summary: Chiang Mai’s Sunday Walking Street turns Ratchadamnoen Road in the Old City into a roughly one-kilometre pedestrian market between Tha Phae Gate and Wat Phra Singh, with craft and souvenir stalls, street food, temple courtyards and performers. It is a lively, very crowded evening outing rather than a quick browse.
whyGo: Browse a broad mix of northern Thai handicrafts, clothes, souvenirs and street food along the Old City’s main historic road.
Use temple courtyards as informal food courts and take a break from the moving crowd.
Combine the market with an afternoon visit to Old City temples; the route passes several religious compounds.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want one concentrated evening of Chiang Mai food, shopping and people-watching
Travellers staying in or near the Old City who can walk the route
Visitors happy to browse without a fixed shopping list and tolerate dense crowds
skipIf: You dislike shoulder-to-shoulder crowds or need a calm, spacious market visit.
You need reliably step-free access, seating or accessible toilets throughout; these are not documented in the sources reviewed.
You want a weekday market or specialist craft shopping; the Night Bazaar is open nightly, while Saturday’s Wualai market has a stronger silver tradition.
duration: Planning estimate: 2–3 hours to walk a substantial section, eat and browse; the full route is about 1 km each way, and pauses or crowds can extend the visit.
cost: No admission fee is listed; budget separately for food, drinks, transport and purchases. Total spend depends on what you eat and buy; prices vary by stall, so carry small baht notes and check prices before ordering.
hours: Chiang Mai Province’s tourism page lists Sunday hours of about 17:00–22:00. Arrive after stalls begin setting up; hours and individual stall times can vary.
bestTime: For more room to browse, arrive around 17:00. The busiest period is typically about 19:00–21:00, especially in the cool season and on holiday weekends. Go later for a shorter food-focused visit, with some stalls potentially closing.
gettingThere: The route runs along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate west to Wat Phra Singh. Walk from accommodation in the Old City if practical. The road is closed to vehicles during the market, so arrange a ride-hail or songthaew drop-off outside the pedestrian zone and agree the pick-up point away from the crowds.
booking: No booking is needed for the public street market. It is a weekly Sunday market; check locally for exceptional closures or road arrangements before travelling.
accessibility: The market occupies a public road, but stalls, uneven pavement edges and dense moving crowds can make navigation difficult. The sources reviewed do not confirm step-free routes, accessible toilets, seating or crowd-free entry. Visit near opening for more space and confirm specific access needs locally.
practicalTips: Choose a meeting point in advance; mobile service and finding companions can be difficult in the busiest stretch.
Keep bags in front of you in the crush, carry small cash and check stall prices before ordering.
Step into temple courtyards for food and a pause; dress respectfully and follow signs at active religious sites.
If the Sunday crowd is too much, consider Saturday’s Wualai market or the nightly Night Bazaar instead.
decemberNotes: December falls in Chiang Mai’s popular cool season, so expect a busy Sunday evening and plan for cooler conditions after dark; this is seasonal guidance, not a forecast. Sundays in December 2026 fall on 6, 13, 20 and 27 December. The first date overlaps the Chiang Mai Design Week period noted elsewhere in the trip plan, which may add activity and demand; verify the festival programme and any market changes closer to travel. No special Christmas or New Year market schedule was confirmed.
uncertainties: The provincial tourism page lists 17:00–22:00, while current independent guidance says stalls generally set up from 16:00–17:00 and wind down around 22:00–23:00; no official detailed timetable was found.
No December 2026 market closure, traffic plan, special event schedule or vendor-level details were confirmed.
Accessibility facilities and conditions vary along the route and were not specified by the sources reviewed.
